section_summary: This section of State Department decimal file 894.001 covers political and administrative matters concerning the Japanese Emperor, Imperial Household, and related regional affairs from August 1945 to October 1948. It includes analyses of State Shinto and the imperial institution, policy discussions between SCAP and Washington regarding Emperor Hirohito's potential prosecution for war crimes or abdication, and arrangements for appointing Elizabeth Gray Vining as American tutor to Crown Prince Akihito. In addition, the file contains misfiled military and State Department records concerning travel arrangements and air priority disputes for Korean political leader Syngman Rhee, as well as inquiries regarding royal visits and public reception of the Emperor.

subfiles.about: Linebarger transmits an academic paper by Professor Homer H. Dubs concerning the Japanese Emperor and State Shinto.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Dubs's proposals to replace Hirohito with an older collateral successor and temporarily display the Three Sacred Treasures.
subfiles.title: Letter from Paul M. A. Linebarger to Joseph C. Grew Transmitting Manuscript by Homer H. Dubs

subfiles.about: Grew thanks Linebarger for forwarding Homer H. Dubs's paper on the Japanese imperial cult.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt of Dubs's paper, promising careful departmental study, and thanks Linebarger for generous personal remarks.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph C. Grew to Paul M. A. Linebarger Acknowledging Receipt of Dubs Paper

subfiles.about: Dubs examines the ideological basis of the Japanese imperial cult and recommends reforms to secure genuine Japanese democratization.
subfiles.summary: Dubs analyzes the ideological foundations of the Japanese state, arguing that State Shinto and imperial divinity underpin militarism and aggression. He contends that lasting democratization requires demonstrating the violability of the emperor and discrediting Shinto deities. To achieve this, he proposes removing Hirohito in favor of an older collateral successor and temporarily displaying the Three Sacred Treasures in Allied capitals.
subfiles.title: The Japanese Emperor and His Cult

subfiles.about: Internal State Department charge slip recording the checkout of an FE memorandum by Vincent.
subfiles.summary: Records the charge of memorandum 894.001/9-2745 by Vincent from the Far Eastern Affairs division.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip for FE Memorandum by Vincent

subfiles.about: Reports a TASS article disputing Prime Minister Shidehara's statement exonerating Emperor Hirohito from war responsibility.
subfiles.summary: Relays a TASS report citing pre-war imperial conferences where Hirohito failed to oppose military preparations against Britain and America.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 4096 from Moscow on Soviet Press Report Regarding Imperial War Responsibility

subfiles.about: Tracks the loan of document 894.001/6-2446 concerning a letter to Vincent.
subfiles.summary: Charge-out slip recording file 894.001/6-2446 charged out to Reid.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Out Slip for Letter to Vincent

subfiles.about: Stoddard notifies Benton of the Imperial Household's decision to appoint Elizabeth Gray Vining as tutor to Crown Prince Akihito.
subfiles.summary: Confirms Mrs. Vining's selection and acceptance as tutor to Crown Prince Akihito, describes her qualifications, and requests guidance on communications.
subfiles.title: Letter from George D. Stoddard to William Benton Regarding Selection of Tutor for Crown Prince

subfiles.about: Military cable relaying the Japanese Imperial Household's choice of Elizabeth Gray Vining as royal tutor.
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Army Forces in the Pacific (CINCAFPAC)
subfiles.summary: Informs Stoddard that the Imperial Household selected Vining as tutor and requests prompt notification of her formal acceptance.
subfiles.title: Telegram from CINCAFPAC to George D. Stoddard Advising Selection of Vining

subfiles.about: Nugent clarifies previous cable transmissions regarding the decision on Mrs. Vining.
subfiles.summary: Advises Stoddard of prior signals sent through War Department Civil Affairs Division regarding the Vining decision.
subfiles.title: Telegram from D. R. Nugent to George D. Stoddard on Vining Appointment Confirmation

subfiles.about: Stoddard congratulates Vining on her appointment and discusses communication and publicity protocols.
subfiles.summary: Informs Vining of her official selection by the Imperial Household and outlines coordination with GHQ SCAP and the State Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from George D. Stoddard to Elizabeth Gray Vining Confirming Selection as Tutor

subfiles.about: Outlines Elizabeth Gray Vining's educational background, teaching career, published writings, and Quaker affiliations.
subfiles.summary: Details Vining's education at Bryn Mawr, teaching experience, literary awards including the Newbery Medal, and Quaker background.
subfiles.title: Biographical Sketch and Curriculum Vitae of Elizabeth Gray Vining

subfiles.about: Draft reply from Benton to Stoddard praising the selection of Vining and commenting on public announcement plans.
subfiles.summary: Draft letter expressing satisfaction with Vining's appointment as royal tutor, containing handwritten revisions regarding publicity.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter from William Benton to George D. Stoddard Regarding Imperial Tutor Appointment

subfiles.about: Bowles submits a suggested draft reply for Benton to Stoddard concerning Vining's appointment.
subfiles.summary: Recommends language for Benton's response to Stoddard regarding the significance of an American tutor and handling publicity.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Gordon T. Bowles to A. T. Curran with Draft Reply to Stoddard

subfiles.about: Bowles provides a revised draft reply incorporating instructions on coordinating travel via the War Department.
subfiles.summary: Proposes revised reply directing Stoddard to contact the Civil Affairs Division for travel logistics and promising immediate press release.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Gordon T. Bowles to A. T. Curran with Revised Reply to Stoddard

subfiles.about: Transmits the Vining file back to Bowles for further revisions.
subfiles.summary: Returns the file on Mrs. Vining to Bowles for additional drafting changes as requested.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip from A. T. Curran to Gordon T. Bowles Returning Vining File

subfiles.about: Curran asks Bowles whether Assistant Secretary Benton should issue a press release from the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Requests guidance on whether the State Department should issue an official press release regarding the imperial tutor.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip from A. T. Curran to Gordon T. Bowles Inquiring on Press Release

subfiles.about: Stoddard encloses letters from Nugent and to Vining, urging Benton to release a public statement.
subfiles.summary: Encloses correspondence regarding Vining's appointment terms and urges Benton to make an immediate public announcement, withholding financial details.
subfiles.title: Letter from George D. Stoddard to William Benton Urging Public Announcement

subfiles.about: Stoddard informs Vining of the living, financial, and household arrangements being made for her in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Reassures Vining about her salary and household accommodations in Tokyo based on Nugent's letter, noting impending public announcement.
subfiles.title: Letter from George D. Stoddard to Elizabeth Gray Vining Outlining Travel and Living Arrangements

subfiles.about: Nugent specifies the administrative status, compensation, accommodations, and instructional duties arranged for Vining in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Outlines Vining's status under the Imperial Household Ministry, detailing residence, staff, transportation, dollar compensation, and instructional responsibilities for Crown Prince Akihito alongside Japanese tutors and British educator Blyth.
subfiles.title: Letter from D. R. Nugent to George D. Stoddard Detailing Terms of Imperial Tutor Appointment

subfiles.about: Bowles recommends forwarding correspondence on Vining to Major Simmons of the Civil Affairs Division.
subfiles.summary: Suggests sending attached letters to Major Simmons of the Civil Affairs Division to expedite Vining's travel arrangements.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Gordon T. Bowles to A. T. Curran Recommending Notice to War Department

subfiles.about: Informational copy of Stoddard's letter to Vining provided to Gordon T. Bowles.
subfiles.summary: Confidential copy of Stoddard's August 10 letter to Vining confirming her appointment, provided for Bowles's information.
subfiles.title: Copy of Letter from George D. Stoddard to Elizabeth Gray Vining

subfiles.about: Requests filing of miscellaneous papers concerning efforts to obtain return transportation for Syngman Rhee.
subfiles.summary: Directs filing of papers concerning efforts to secure return transportation to Korea for Dr. Rhee following his departure.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Assistant Secretary to Mr. Conger Regarding Syngman Rhee Transportation Files

subfiles.about: Summarizes the State Department's denial of military air priority to Syngman Rhee due to lack of national interest.
subfiles.summary: Reviews the decision denying Rhee Air Transport Command priority because private travel was not deemed in the national interest.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from J. K. Penfield to Dudley G. Cameron on Rhee's ATC Priority Application

subfiles.about: New York Times article reporting State Department facilitation of commercial air passage for Syngman Rhee after Army refusal.
subfiles.summary: Reports that the State Department assisted Syngman Rhee in booking commercial flight passage to Korea via China after the War Department cancelled his military air priority.
subfiles.title: Newspaper Clipping: 'Rhee Gets Passage for Trip to Korea' by Bertram D. Hulen

subfiles.about: Details the inter-departmental investigation and cancellation of unauthorized military air transport for Syngman Rhee.
subfiles.summary: Chronicles the discovery that unauthorized ATC reservations were issued for Syngman Rhee contrary to General Hodge's warnings, and describes how War Department and State Department officials coordinated to revoke the priority and establish consistent policy.
subfiles.title: Confidential Memorandum for the Record by Lt. Col. Dupuy on Cancellation of Rhee's Air Priority

subfiles.about: Draft statement explaining the lack of War and State Department clearance for military transportation for Dr. Rhee.
subfiles.summary: Outlines War Department policy restricting military air transport for private Korean citizens lacking official State Department priority clearance.
subfiles.title: Draft State Department Policy Statement on Dr. Rhee's Military Transportation

subfiles.about: Reports questions asked in the House of Commons by Skeffington-Lodge regarding Hirohito's reception in Hiroshima and Emperor worship.
subfiles.summary: Transmits parliamentary exchange between Skeffington-Lodge and Minister McNeil concerning Hirohito's popular reception at Hiroshima and prevention of Emperor worship.
subfiles.title: Incoming Airgram No. 2531 from London on British Parliamentary Exchange Regarding Emperor Worship

subfiles.about: Records the charge-out of Tokyo Despatch 771 filed under 894.001/5-3147.
subfiles.summary: Charge-out slip for Despatch 771 from Tokyo, charged to Goodwin.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Out Slip for Tokyo Despatch 771

subfiles.about: Relays MacArthur's belief that Hirohito must not abdicate or commit suicide following the International Military Tribunal verdict.
subfiles.summary: Reports MacArthur's firm conviction that imperial abdication following the war crimes trial verdicts would be politically disastrous and foster communism.
subfiles.title: Letter from W. J. Sebald to H. Merrell Benninghoff on MacArthur's Views Regarding Imperial Abdication

subfiles.about: Clarifies that Hirohito never visited the United States, though his brothers Princes Chichibu and Takamatsu did.
subfiles.summary: Informs Mrs. Ross that Emperor Hirohito never visited America, suggesting the newspaper photograph depicted one of his royal brothers.
subfiles.title: Letter from Erle R. Dickover to Mrs. E. E. Ross Clarifying Imperial Family Visits to the US

subfiles.about: Local news story recounting how Mrs. John T. Shirley photographed a Japanese prince at Harpers Ferry two decades earlier.
subfiles.summary: Describes Mrs. John T. Shirley photographing a young Japanese royal prince at the Harpers Ferry train station twenty years earlier.
subfiles.title: Newspaper Clipping: 'Hirohito Posed at Harpers Ferry'

subfiles.about: Inquires about the historical accuracy of a newspaper clipping claiming Emperor Hirohito visited the United States.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a newspaper clipping and asks the State Department when Emperor Hirohito made his reported visit to the United States.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mrs. E. E. Ross Inquiring About Reported US Visit by Hirohito

subfiles.about: Directs MacArthur to assemble evidence regarding Hirohito's potential war criminal culpability under strict security.
subfiles.summary: Instructs MacArthur that Hirohito is not immune from prosecution, ordering covert collection of evidence regarding his war culpability for SWNCC consideration.
subfiles.title: Classified Telegram WARX 85811 from Joint Chiefs of Staff to MacArthur on Hirohito War Crimes Evidence

subfiles.about: Transmits Atcheson's confidential memorandum to MacArthur analyzing policy options regarding Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch transmitting Atcheson's memorandum to MacArthur concerning policy choices regarding the imperial institution and war crimes trial.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 180 from George Atcheson, Jr. Transmitting Memorandum on Status and Future of Emperor

subfiles.about: Analyzes whether the United States should try Hirohito as a war criminal or retain him to ensure stable administration and constitutional reform.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson outlines two major policy paths for the United States regarding Emperor Hirohito in light of upcoming Far Eastern Commission scrutiny. While acknowledging that true democratization ultimately requires ending the imperial institution and prosecuting Hirohito, he recommends a cautious policy of retaining and utilizing him. He argues that preserving the throne maintains popular stability, assists occupation administration, and enables necessary constitutional revisions.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by George Atcheson, Jr. on the Status and Future of the Emperor

subfiles.about: Transmits MacArthur's cable strongly advising against prosecuting Hirohito as a war criminal.
subfiles.summary: Transmits MacArthur's negative appraisal regarding prosecuting Hirohito as a war criminal, highlighting pertinent passages for Acheson's review.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from John Carter Vincent to Dean Acheson on MacArthur's Opposition to Trying Hirohito

subfiles.about: MacArthur warns that indicting Hirohito would destroy Japanese national cohesion, provoke guerrilla resistance, and require massive occupation forces.
subfiles.summary: Reports that extensive investigation uncovered no tangible evidence of Hirohito initiating aggressive policies, his role being largely ministerial. MacArthur warns that indicting the Emperor would trigger violent convulsion, civil disintegration, and potential guerrilla warfare, necessitating at least one million occupation troops.
subfiles.title: Classified Telegram CA 57235 from Douglas MacArthur Warning Against Prosecuting Hirohito
